problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the matrix $[T]_{B}$ of a linear transformation $T$ with respect to this basis. Find the matrix of $T$ relative to the standard basis $S.$

activity_context.topic_title: Connections Between Matrix Representations of a Linear Transformation

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to the Standard Basis
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/fe3c67c0218808ba7b398d1659530d61a4c8ce3eafd196341ba6645ac7076f43.png)

Consider the basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}}$ of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with respect to this basis. Find the matrix of $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the standard basis $\mathcal{S}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ and standard basis $\mathcal{S}$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/dbd020362f950fe8bfb4c592652b9e78a73610fa01a247b0b7ead6f201bf9ea5.png)

 

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{S}} = P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{S}}} \cdot [\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}} \cdot P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{S}}}^{-1},
$$

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/d050ac7d04af79ad9b5e7f096e3d21c9808af4a756f43d46ca29beca00dedcc9.png)

First, we compute the inverse of $P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{S}}} \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{B\to S}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & -7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 3-(-7)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the matrix of $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the standard basis $\mathcal{S} \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T]_{S} & ={P}_{B\to S}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 13 \\ 3 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 11 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
[T]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $[T]_{B}$ of a linear transformation $T$ with respect to the basis $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ shown above. Find the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $C.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/1b81504d6fdcabee0e1f586fef3dd2af5a57a8411ba4d22429e00e09b171a4d1.png)

 

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[T]_{C}={P}_{B\to C}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{B\to C}^{-1}\,,
$$

where ${P}_{B\to C}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C.$

Our goal is to compute $[T]_{C}.$ First, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{B\to C}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 1-4\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 18 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
